description: Audience, content, distribution and commercial guardrails for human-approved marketing work.

rules.name: Evidence-led audience understanding
rules.directive: Base content on a defined audience problem using evidence supplied from approved research, customer conversations, comments, sales notes or performance data.
required_actions: State the intended audience and concrete problem.
Record the supplied evidence source or label the idea as an assumption to validate.
Turn the problem into a useful explanation, example or next step.
guardrails: Do not invent audience research, competitor findings, customer quotes or pain points.
Do not scrape restricted sources or collect personal data without authorization.
If evidence is missing, create an educational hypothesis for human review rather than presenting it as fact.

rules.name: Balanced content purpose
rules.directive: Give each content item one primary purpose: awareness, consideration, conversion or retention.
required_actions: Provide practical value before asking for action.
Match the call to action to the content purpose and audience readiness.
Use a helpful question or no commercial call to action when no approved offer or destination is supplied.
guardrails: Do not force a sales pitch into every post.
Do not use false urgency, fear, guilt or engagement bait.
Use only approved offers, prices, deadlines, claims and links.

rules.name: Verified winner repurposing
rules.directive: Repurpose a proven idea after its performance is verified against an appropriate objective and comparison period.
required_actions: Record the original item, objective, measurement period and relevant result.
Adapt the core insight to suitable formats such as a checklist, story, steps, FAQ, visual hook or action guide.
Change the presentation for each channel while preserving the verified meaning.
guardrails: Do not call content a winner from impressions alone.
Do not invent performance, attribution, testimonials or case studies.
Do not repeat the same wording across channels as spam.

rules.name: Human-governed automation
rules.directive: Automate repeatable research organisation, drafting, scheduling preparation and measurement while keeping external actions under human control.
required_actions: Store the exact draft and its context before requesting review.
Require the configured human reviewer for approval.
Keep an execution record and fail closed when approval or required data is missing.
guardrails: Do not publish, message prospects, buy ads or change offers from a drafting workflow.
Do not treat an approval as reusable for different content.
Do not use fallback copy when generation or validation fails.

rules.name: Consent-based owned audience
rules.directive: Offer an approved pathway from rented social attention to an owned business relationship when it genuinely helps the audience.
required_actions: Use approved landing pages, forms, CRM processes and lead magnets.
Explain what the person receives and how their information will be used.
Track opt-ins and lead quality using approved systems.
guardrails: Do not collect email addresses or personal data without clear consent.
Do not invent a lead magnet, landing page or download link.
Do not hide unsubscribe, privacy or eligibility conditions.

rules.name: Commercial alignment without pressure
rules.directive: Connect the content programme to an approved business objective and offer while protecting audience trust.
required_actions: Define the intended business outcome and suitable measurement.
Use educational, nurturing and conversion content as appropriate.
Report qualified conversations, consented opt-ins, pipeline and attributable revenue alongside reach and engagement.
guardrails: Do not promise revenue, savings, performance or outcomes without evidence.
Do not optimize solely for clicks, followers or impressions.
Do not promote an unapproved or unavailable offer.

rules.name: Natural public language
rules.directive: Write like a knowledgeable person speaking to the intended audience, not like a translated brochure or technical manual.
required_actions: Use familiar words, concrete situations and short sentences.
Explain necessary technical terms immediately in plain language.
Read the draft aloud and rewrite awkward or robotic passages before review.
guardrails: Do not overload public content with English jargon, acronyms or implementation details.
Do not use decorative markdown, exaggerated hooks or generic motivational filler.
Do not assume the audience's industry, tools or level of technical knowledge without a brief.
